m061: Where do I make my first application in Korea?

m064: Track your permitted stay separately from the review
m065: An ongoing refugee review and administrative procedures such as extending your permitted stay are separate matters. If you want to stay beyond your permitted period, check the extension procedure before it expires.
m067: If you received a refusal notice
m068: Under Article 21 of the Refugee Act, an objection must be filed within 30 days of receiving the relevant notice. The date the decision was written may differ from the date you received it. Check the method and deadline in the notice and contact a legal support organization. Confirm your own deadline using your notice and legal advice.
m070: Objections and lawsuits have different deadlines
m071: As a general rule, an action for revocation must be brought within 90 days of learning of the disposition, etc., and within 1 year of the disposition, etc. The starting date needs to be checked based on the route taken, service of the notice and other circumstances. Do not assume that a lawsuit is only possible after an objection; seek advice for your situation.
m073: What should I check if I move?
m074: Registered foreign residents should check the requirement to report a change of residence within 15 days of moving to a new address. Also check that the reviewing authority has your updated address and contact details.
m076: If you do not understand something in the interview
m077: There are rules on interpretation when you cannot express yourself sufficiently in Korean, checking the interview record in a language you understand, and inspecting or copying materials and interview records. Ask for the support you need. Inspection and copying may be restricted for reasons specified by law.
m078: Refugee Act rules on interviews and records
m079: If you find it difficult to complete the application alone
m080: There are rules requiring assistance from the receiving official if you cannot complete the application because of illiteracy, disability or similar reasons. Using this app is not the only way to apply, and you can ask for help if needed.
m082: Can I start working 6 months after applying?
m083: Work permission is not granted automatically once 6 months have passed since your refugee application. If you want to work, check the requirements and procedure for prior permission with 1345 or the responsible office. Support programs may also differ for applicants, recognized refugees and humanitarian status holders.
m084: UNHCR guidance on applicants' rights and treatment
m085: How are my personal information and records handled?
m086: The Refugee Act prohibits disclosure or release of personal details without consent and provision of application-related information to the country of origin. Separately check how the app stores and sends data. This prototype does not send records to a server. It automatically saves your progress answers, document statuses and checked items in this browser without encryption. You can delete saved records using Reset under More. Manage any files you backed up separately.

m321: How this prototype differs from MAP
m322: DARI is a procedure guide prototype that helps refugee applicants confirm the notices they received and steps they actually took, then find the preparations, documents and organization information needed at their current place in the overall process.
